rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body; this is a narrative lecture, not an interactive demo beat.

chunk 5 header 'You just ran the compound loop' holds against the reworded body: 'same shape, more names' affirms one loop under two labelings, same singular claim the header makes, and more directly than the retired 'the names differ, the loop doesn't' did. All other headers match their chunk content.

RE-JUDGED. Prior REVISE targeted line 43's retired clause 'the names differ, the loop doesn't', reading it as a 'Number + own retraction' hedge stretched from a single number to a sequence-count (four-token loop vs eight-token loop reconciled by bare assertion). The replacement, 'same shape, more names', does not fit that sub-item on a plain read: it is a flat equivalence claim, not a stated-then-undercut number — nothing is retracted, no hedge word ('roughly', 'could be more or less', 'give or take') appears, and no specific count is asserted and then walked back. It reads as a structural claim (the eight named stages are a finer cut of the same four-stage shape), which is what the sentence actually says. Rest of the rule checked clean across all six chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; chunk 1's triple ('Some were overscoped. Some fired on the wrong passage. Some held for one kind of content and broke for another') has a third leg carrying new concrete content (content-type failure, distinct from breadth and placement) and passes the third-leg test; no self-grading superlatives; no abstraction-noun stacks; no verb triplets with an empty leg. Independent of the maintainer's decision to keep the sequence (recorded in the backing block, and echoed in check_writing.md #11 / check_pedagogy.md §14 carve-outs added for the writing/pedagogy classes) — on check_slides.md's own rule 7 text, the reworded line simply no longer has the shape the rule bans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: RE-JUDGED. chunk 1 "Wrong is how steering gets in": line 13: "Some fired on the wrong passage." — the prior flag named two stacked dialect terms ('fired' + 'surface'); 'surface' is gone, but 'fired' survives alone and still trips this rule on its own. The compendium's own illustrative list of banned maintainer dialect names 'firing' verbatim, alongside 'compendium' and 'forcing function' — not a borderline case needing inference. Unlike 'surface', which the compendium explicitly carves out for ordinary-verb use ('surface the issue'), rule 8 gives 'firing'/'fired' no equivalent carve-out for a non-jargon sense, and none applies here: the subject of the sentence is 'the rules' (this training's own compendium rules), and 'fired' is used in exactly the sense content-rules.md ('Fires when…') and this very compendium ('Fires PER CHUNK') use it — a rule activating on a passage. That is the jargon meaning applied to its jargon referent, not a homograph escaping into ordinary English (contrast 'the engine fired', which isn't present). A student with no access to the compendium/rule-firing system cannot parse 'fired on the wrong passage' as 'applied to the wrong kind of writing' without already knowing this repo's internal vocabulary for rule activation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast without 'fired' — e.g. 'Some applied to the wrong kind of writing' or 'Some didn't fit the passage they were meant for' — same plain-English swap already made for 'surface'.
